name: Abiasaph
overview: Abiasaph was a male member of the tribe of Levi, uniquely identified as the son of Korah. Notably, he survived the rebellion associated with his father, as recorded in the book of Numbers. His lineage places him within the Levitical priestly family, which held significant religious responsibilities in Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Abiasaph means '[my] father has gathered,' reflecting a familial or covenantal gathering. This name appears also as Ebiasaph in Scripture, carrying the same meaning. Neither form of the name is indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Abiasaph as the son of Korah. Additionally, there is an inferred relationship that Kore is his father, based on genealogical records. Beyond these connections, no other family relationships are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Abiasaph's significance lies in his survival of the rebellion connected to Korah, which was a pivotal event demonstrating God's judgment and mercy within the Levitical family. His survival ensured the continuation of the Korahite lineage, which played important roles in Israel's worship and temple service. Thus, Abiasaph represents both a link in the priestly heritage and a testimony to God's preservation of His chosen line.
